trust_decision.summary: In webdav mode the single verb guard in SetupMux blocks PUT/MKCOL/MOVE/COPY only under ReadOnly and blocks DELETE under ReadOnly||UploadOnly||NoDelete, so with --no-delete a MOVE (Rename, which removes the source and RemoveAll()s an existing destination) and an overwriting COPY (RemoveAll() of the destination) still delete files; every WebDAV verb passes through this one guard.

landing_point.why: The summary names MOVE; this is the 'http.MethodPut, MKCOL, MOVE, COPY' branch of the only place the WebDAV mode flags are enforced (the wdGuard closure at httpserver/server.go:237-263).

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP WebDAV mux route: mux.Handle("/", wdGuard) installed in SetupMux(mux, "webdav") at httpserver/server.go:270
same WebDAV mux route; the added webdavGuard/webdavDestExists replace the inline closure at httpserver/server.go:237-263

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and its fix are about the WebDAV server; FTP is a separate protocol in another package that already has its own --no-delete wrapper (afero noDeleteFs), so its rename gap reads as that wrapper's problem rather than this advisory's.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A COPY to a path that does not yet exist deletes nothing and must stay allowed under --no-delete (Overwrite defaults to on, so only the 'destination already exists' case is a deletion); likewise a plain MOVE with no mode flag set must keep working.

O6_input_shapes: MOVE with Overwrite: T onto an existing destination
COPY with Overwrite default/T onto an existing destination
COPY with Overwrite: F and COPY to a fresh path (must remain allowed)
DELETE on a file or a collection
Destination header as absolute URL, encoded path, existing vs missing target

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SMB2 SET_INFO FileRenameInformation renames (and can overwrite) a file while --no-delete is set; only UploadOnly is checked, the adjacent FileDisposition case checks NoDelete
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: SMB is a separate server with its own delete gating (FileDispositionInformation at smbserver/server.go:2171-2187 and delete-on-close at smbserver/server.go:1377-1390); rename is ordinary file management, and the advisory names WebDAV MOVE.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 2 packages (smbserver imports httpserver); different file and different transport

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Enforce ReadOnly/UploadOnly/NoDelete inside webdavACLFileSystem.RemoveAll and Rename, next to the existing aclError check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The wrapper already intercepts exactly the two primitives MOVE and overwriting COPY use, and the .goshs ACL is deliberately enforced both here and at the mux (httpserver/webdav_acl.go:36-61); a maintainer hardening after this bypass would naturally add the mode flags at the FileSystem layer too.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Gate FileRenameInformation on s.NoDelete the same way FileDispositionInformation is gated
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The neighbouring case already checks s.NoDelete for deletes, so extending the same condition to rename is a one-line change a maintainer could ship.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A no-delete handler/wrapper for SFTP Filecmd Rename/Rmdir/Remove, mirroring the ReadOnlyHandler/UploadOnlyHandler in sftpserver/handler.go
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: SFTP is the alternate backend behind --ftp and already has per-mode handler variants (sftpserver/handler.go:11-80); a maintainer extending --no-delete to it would copy that pattern.
